newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy to pay pensions arrears in cash.
newsitem.headline: Italy to pay pensions arrears in cash.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government said on Monday it would pay in cash back-dated state pensions affecting more than one million people, rather than use special Treasury bonds as originally planned.
But Treasury undersecretary Giorgio Macciotta said the switch would not weigh on public accounts.
Tranches due to be paid out for 1996 and 1997 amounted to 7.34 trillion lire, he said.

The decision was contained within a maxi-amendment on the 1997 mini-budget on which the government has called a confidence vote for Tuesday afternoon. The do-or-die test is designed to sweep away hundreds of opposition amendments and speed passage of the controversial package.

The complex court rulings on the payouts were made in 1993 and 1994 and state pensions body Inps has estimated they would cost between 19.7 trillion lire ($12.69 billion) and 47.3 trillion lire to cover.
The constitutional court decreed that people receiving minimum pensions had been denied certain benefits since 1983 and ordered that these be repaid.
